<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
def get_player_pos():
    seg = current_frame.segmentation
    for n in seg['nodes']:
        if n['pixels'] == 24:
            b = n['boundary']
            rows = [p[0] for p in b]
            cols = [p[1] for p in b]
            return (min(rows), min(cols))
    return None

# BFS to map the maze
# Start from current position [20,26]
start = get_player_pos()
print(f"Start: {start}")

# Build adjacency map
visited = {start}
queue = [start]
adj = {}

# We need to navigate to each position and test all 4 directions
# But this is expensive. Let me use the state graph instead.

# Actually, let me just explore systematically from current position
# Go UP to [14,26] and test all directions from there
result = action(['UP'])
pos = get_player_pos()
print(f"\nAt {pos}, testing all directions:")

for direction in ['UP', 'DOWN', 'LEFT', 'RIGHT']:
    result = action([direction])
    new_pos = get_player_pos()
    moved = new_pos != pos
    print(f"  {direction}: {pos} -> {new_pos}, moved={moved}")
    if moved:
        pos = new_pos

# Now explore from new positions
# Go back to [14,26] first
result = action(['UP'])
pos = get_player_pos()
print(f"\nBack at {pos}")

# Try RIGHT from [14,26]
result = action(['RIGHT'])
pos = get_player_pos()
print(f"RIGHT: -> {pos}, moved={pos != (14,26)}")

# Try RIGHT again
result = action(['RIGHT'])
pos = get_player_pos()
print(f"RIGHT: -> {pos}, moved={pos != (14,32)}")

# Try DOWN from current
result = action(['DOWN'])
pos = get_player_pos()
print(f"DOWN: -> {pos}, moved={pos != (14,32) if pos[0]==14 else pos != (14,32)}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
